claims.statement: BootMode (fresh / snapshot_restore / repo_image / build) is derived from process env in runtime_config.py: IMAGE_BUILD_MODE=true → build, RESTORED_FROM_SNAPSHOT=true → snapshot_restore, FROM_REPO_IMAGE=true → repo_image, otherwise fresh; the supervisor stamps OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE into the environment so hooks and child processes branch on it.

entrypoint.py is the composition root: it consumes process secrets, builds RuntimeConfig, and composes RepositoryBoot, ManagedSkillsMaterializer, OpenCodeServer, AgentBridgeProcess, CodeServer, WebTerminal, and BrowserDesktop into one SandboxSupervisor; SIGTERM/SIGINT are routed into a supervisor-owned asyncio shutdown event.

SandboxSupervisor.run() boots in strict order: prepare tunnel environment, start VNC desktop (best-effort), repository boot (manifest write -> credential config -> git sync -> setup/start hooks -> workspace manifest), managed-skills materialization, code-server, web terminal, OpenCode server, then the bridge subprocess, followed by monitor_processes().

The supervisor applies an explicit per-component restart policy with max 5 restarts and 2^n backoff capped at 60 s (monitor_processes); exceeding the cap for OpenCode or the bridge reports a fatal sandbox error, while code-server/terminal/VNC caps degrade to warnings; a bridge exit code of 0 is treated as graceful and shuts the whole sandbox down.

Fatal supervisor errors are POSTed to /sessions/{session_id}/sandbox-error with the sandbox token (Authorization Bearer + X-Sandbox-ID), retried up to 3 times with 2^n backoff, message truncated to 1000 chars.
Shutdown stops services in reverse start order: bridge, web terminal, code-server, browser desktop, then OpenCode; a pending desktop restart task is cancelled first.

The agent bridge runs as its own subprocess (python -m sandbox_runtime.bridge) spawned by AgentBridgeProcess with sandbox-id/session-id/control-plane URL/token/opencode-port arguments, so a bridge crash cannot take down OpenCode and vice versa.

The bridge connects to wss://{control_plane}/sessions/{session_id}/ws?type=sandbox with Authorization: Bearer {sandbox_token} and X-Sandbox-ID headers; it sends a heartbeat event every 30 s and reconnects with exponential backoff (base 2 s, cap 60 s).

Bridge connection errors matching HTTP 401/403/404/410 raise SessionTerminatedError and are not retried (the session is invalid or terminated); the bridge exits gracefully so the control plane can restore the session from a snapshot on the next prompt.

On connect the bridge sends a ready event carrying sandboxId, the persisted opencodeSessionId, the image-baked SANDBOX_VERSION runtime version (stamped onto snapshots for compatibility), and the repo manifest positions with repoOwner/repoName/baseSha for each repository that has a base sha.

Supervisor boot warnings are queued to /tmp/oi-boot-warnings.jsonl (JSONL {scope, message, repoOwner?, repoName?}) because the supervisor has no control-plane event channel; the bridge drains the file exactly once after the WebSocket handshake into warning sandbox events, so reconnects never replay it.

Prompt commands run as background tasks NOT tracked in the per-connection background-task set, so a prompt survives WebSocket disconnects while the bridge reconnects; on completion the task's done-callback emits execution_complete (success or error) and requests an idle diff refresh.

Prompt duration is budgeted to leave snapshot headroom: prompt_max_duration_seconds = sandbox_timeout_seconds minus min(900 s, 25% of the timeout), where the sandbox timeout defaults to 7200 s and is overridable via SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; the SSE inactivity timeout default is 120 s clamped to [5, 3600] via BRIDGE_SSE_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT.

Sandbox events are delivered through BufferedEventForwarder: while no connection is bound (or a send fails) events buffer (max 1000, evicting non-critical events first); critical event types (execution_complete, error, snapshot_ready, push_complete, push_error) carry a deterministic ackId ({type}:{messageId}, else {type}:{random}) and stay pending until the control plane sends an ack command, so they are re-sent on reconnect; bind() recovers the backlog under one lock so a concurrent drain and bind never both walk the buffer.

The push command normalizes the provider's pushSpec into PushRequest (missing fields become ""/False), validates structure (both or neither of repoOwner/repoName, branch, refspec, push_url), resolves the checkout through the supervisor-written repo manifest (a spec-named member is matched and its path used verbatim so crafted names cannot select a checkout outside the session; identity-less specs use the sole /workspace clone), runs git push as an argument array capped at 300 s (terminate then kill after 5 s grace), redacts credential-bearing URLs from stderr, and funnels every failure into a single push_error emitter that includes branchName even when empty.

The git credential helper implements git's credential protocol and mints fresh short-lived SCM credentials on every get from the control plane endpoint /sessions/{session_id}/scm-credentials; it refuses to serve credentials unless protocol is https and the requested host equals the configured VCS_HOST (default github.com), so a malicious submodule URL or git ls-remote against an attacker host cannot exfiltrate the installation token.

A successful credential-helper response is cached to /run/oi/scm-creds.json (mode 0600, atomic write, advisory flock serializing concurrent first-boot get calls) and reused only while more than 5 minutes of TTL remain; the cache is never a fallback for a failed refresh — a control-plane rejection exits non-zero because stale tokens silently authenticating are worse than visible failures.

The credential helper falls back to the injected VCS_CLONE_TOKEN env (username x-access-token unless VCS_CLONE_USERNAME set, 1-hour TTL) only when no control-plane context exists at all; partial control-plane context refuses the fallback.

The credential helper's gh-token action prints a fresh token for the gh wrapper only when the environment has no genuine user token (GH_TOKEN always wins, then GITHUB_TOKEN/GITHUB_APP_TOKEN, with OI_GITHUB_TOKEN_IS_FALLBACK=1 marking the expiring system fallback); a failed mint prints nothing and exits 0 so gh falls through to its existing env, and non-github deployments never touch gh's own auth.

GitSigningRuntime fetches the session commit-signing configuration from GET /sessions/{id}/commit-signing and applies it per repository with local git config: enabled -> gpg.format=ssh, gpg.ssh.program=<oi-git-sign>, user.signingkey=key::<ed25519 key>, commit.gpgsign=true plus committer/author identity; disabled -> signing keys unset and identity defaulted to OpenInspect <open-inspect@noreply.github.com> unless the prompt supplied an attributed user.

Git signing configuration fetch errors are retryable only for HTTP 408/429/5xx and transport errors; a non-retryable GitSigningError stops the bridge run loop (it never degrades silently), and GitSigningError messages never include secret configuration values.

oi-git-sign (git_signer.py) is the stateless gpg.ssh.program: it intercepts git's -Y sign -n git -f invocation, reads the bounded commit payload and Ed25519 public key, POSTs them to /sessions/{id}/commit-signing with the SHA256 blob fingerprint, validates the armored SSH SIGNATURE response, and atomically writes the .sig file; any other ssh-keygen invocation is exec'd through to the stock /usr/bin/ssh-keygen.

OpenCodeServer.start() prepares the filesystem (workspace assembly, tools, deps, skills, bin scripts, oauth sentinels, auth proxy plugins, git excludes) then spawns `opencode serve --port 4096 --hostname 0.0.0.0 --print-logs` with OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (model "provider/model", permission allow-all, MCP config), OPENCODE_CLIENT=serve (disables OpenCode's blocking question tool which would hang the headless run), cwd = repo for single-repo sessions or /workspace otherwise, and waits for /global/health with a 30 s timeout.

For multi-repo sessions OpenCodeServer merges member .opencode/ trees into /workspace/.opencode in position order with last-write-wins (warning naming both members), skipping node_modules and __pycache__; the merged tree is rebuilt from scratch on every boot so removed members do not survive snapshot restores, while node_modules is preserved as image-managed state.

Agent tools: bundled .js tool plugins from /app/sandbox_runtime/tools (and the legacy inspect-plugin.js mapped to create-pull-request.js) are copied into .opencode/tool/; tools gated on env vars (slack-notify.js requires AGENT_SLACK_NOTIFY_ENABLED=true) and tools requiring a repository are skipped when inappropriate; pre-staged plugin dependency trees (package.json/package-lock.json/node_modules from /app/opencode-deps) are copied so OpenCode's Npm.install() skips the blocking arborist reify(), and the global-config seed only touches a pristine dir.

Bundled skills from /app/sandbox_runtime/skills are copied into .opencode/skills with symlinks preserved, and standalone bin/ CLIs are installed into ${OPENINSPECT_BIN_INSTALL_DIR} (default /usr/local/bin) chmod 0755 — deliberately not .opencode/tool/, because OpenCode would import() them during tool discovery and execute module-level code.

Every runtime-installed path (tools, skills, plugins) is recorded in a managed info/exclude block (markers # BEGIN/END Open-Inspect runtime assets) via install_runtime_git_excludes so diff capture and git status ignore runtime-owned files; the reconciliation is atomic, keeps user entries untouched, and retains paths that still exist.

When OPENAI_OAUTH_MANAGED or XAI_OAUTH_MANAGED is set, the OpenCode server writes auth.json placeholder entries with refresh "managed-by-control-plane" (temp-file write at mode 0600, atomic rename) and deploys codex-auth-plugin.js / xai-auth-plugin.js plus the shared provider-token-broker.js into .opencode/plugins/.

The supervisor derives the ordered repository list once from SESSION_CONFIG in repo_config.py, validating owner/name as safe namespace/path segments and rejecting duplicates (checkout paths derive from repo_name, so names must be unique), then writes REPO_MANIFEST_FILE_PATH (/tmp/oi-repo-manifest.json) before any child starts; every other consumer — bridge push targeting, the JS create-pull-request tool, and the diff refresh worker — reads that manifest, giving the /workspace checkout layout exactly one authority.

RepositorySynchronizer clones with --depth 100 --branch <branch>, resets origin to a plain https://{vcs_host}/{owner}/{name}.git URL, fetches the branch, and checks out origin/<branch> with -B; git subprocesses run with start_new_session=True and are killed by process group on timeout (clone 300 s, fetch 120 s), and git stderr is redacted of embedded credentials.

Repository sync preserves the checked-out working tree on snapshot_restore boots (only resetting origin and fetching the branch), and resolve_session_diff_baselines keeps supplied base_sha values immutable and discovers the HEAD baseline only on non-restore boots (discover_missing=False on snapshot_restore).

Git sync failures are fatal for fresh/build boots (raising RuntimeError) and degrade to boot warnings for snapshot_restore/repo_image boots ('the checkout may be stale'); setup.sh failures are fatal only in build mode and warnings otherwise; a primary-repo start.sh failure aborts the boot while member-repo start failures are warnings.

Per-repo hooks run .openinspect/setup.sh (fresh/build only, SETUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS default 300) and .openinspect/start.sh (all non-build modes, START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS default 120) via bash with OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE in the environment, own process group, and a 50-line output tail on failure; timeout kills the process group.

TunnelEnvironment reads EXPECTED_TUNNEL_PORTS, clears stale /workspace/.tunnels.env files whose TUNNEL_SANDBOX_ID does not match the current sandbox (snapshot/image leftovers with dead URLs), and waits up to TUNNEL_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 30) for the fresh tunnel URLs before start.sh runs.

Diff capture compares each checkout against an immutable base_sha and runs git strictly with argument arrays (GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, bounded stdout, 20 s command timeout) — repository paths and filenames are never interpolated into a shell command.

Session diff capture produces one bounded bundle (version 1) across all session repositories: tracked changes via git diff --raw -z plus numstat, unmerged paths via --diff-filter=U, untracked files via ls-files --others --exclude-standard filtered by the runtime git-excludes block; per-file render states are renderable / metadata_only / too_large / binary, binary files carry null line counts, submodule entries carry old/new SHAs (all-zero dirty placeholders resolved to the checked-out HEAD), renames/copies normalize to RENAMED, and a staged-deletion plus untracked-file overlay collapses to one MODIFIED record.

Diff capture applies resource ceilings (1000 files, 512 KiB per patch, 1 MiB total capture, 8 MB metadata, 20 s per command) and bounds the encoded bundle to the 1.5 MiB wire limit by shedding patches largest-first (state -> too_large), then trailing metadata records (marked truncated); a bundle that still exceeds the limit raises DiffCaptureError, and a repository that fails capture becomes an 'unavailable' upload entry with a bounded error string so the bundle still uploads atomically.

SessionDiffRefreshWorker coalesces terminal executions into one eventual idle-time checkout refresh: prompt_started() increments an activity generation and holds an idle gate, requests settle only when idle and not superseded by a newer generation/activity (stale attempts are discarded and retried against the current checkout), failure reports go to POST /sessions/{id}/diff/failure, and a 404 from either diff endpoint marks the feature unsupported for the rest of the sandbox's life; the bridge closes the worker with a 5 s bound at shutdown.

ManagedSkillsMaterializer fetches the session skills installation from GET /sessions/{id}/sandbox-skills (paginated 50/page with nextCursor), validates every byte locally and independently of the control plane — schema version 1, safe paths (no .., absolute, backslash, or control chars; depth <= 10, <= 240 bytes), SHA-256 per file, sizeBytes must equal UTF-8 content length, SKILL.md required with a frontmatter name matching the skill name, executables only under scripts/, 5 MiB aggregate session cap — and terminates a paged fetch that promises more but delivers nothing.

Managed skills deploy into the platform-owned global skills directory via a crash-recoverable journaled swap: skills are staged into .managed-skills-staging, the durable journal is written before moving the current tree (destination -> backup -> staging -> destination) with fsync discipline, an interrupted swap is repaired on next boot, and a failure part-way through a paged fetch leaves the previous installation in place.

Managed skill names shadowed by an existing discovered skill (bundled skills, workspace or member-repo .opencode/skills/.claude/skills/.agents/skills, or the user's home discovery paths) are dropped with a logged warning rather than overriding the user's copy; materialization runs once at boot before OpenCode starts and never depends on control-plane availability after boot because OpenCode restarts reuse the tree.

OpenCodePromptStream supplies its own OpenCode-compatible ascending message ID so assistant messages carry parentID pointing at this prompt's user message; MessageAttribution filters other sessions' noise via that parent chain, and after session compaction uses a creation-time fallback comparing time.created against the prompt start boundary — never message-ID ordering, because OpenCode IDs encode a 48-bit truncated timestamp and stop sorting monotonically every ~795 days.

Child sessions (task sub-tasks) are correlated via ChildActivityCorrelator from session.created events and task-tool metadata (including task_id resume); their text tokens are suppressed and non-text events forwarded with isSubtask=true plus childSessionId/taskCallId, and pending child activity is bounded (2000) with corrupt-correlation errors queued for later attribution.

Prompt request bodies translate reasoning_effort per provider: Anthropic adaptive-thinking models (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6/5, claude-opus-4-6..5) get thinking {type: adaptive} plus outputConfig.effort, other Anthropic models a fixed budgetTokens (16000 high, 31999 max), OpenAI reasoningEffort/reasoningSummary, and xAI a variant; a model without a provider prefix defaults to anthropic.

Session image attachments are validated and hydrated with bounded network concurrency: at most 6 per message, MIME allowed image/png/jpeg/gif/webp, max 10 MiB per image, concurrency 2, downloaded base64-encoded as inline data: URLs in OpenCode file parts; invalid or unfetchable attachments surface a non-fatal media warning to the user timeline.

Repo-image build mode reports completion through RepoImageBuildCallback to the control-plane callback URLs with retries (3 attempts, 2^n backoff, 30 s timeout); a partially configured callback environment (some but not all OI_REPO_IMAGE_* vars) aborts the build with a nonzero exit rather than running with completion reporting silently disabled, which would wedge the control-plane row in 'building'.

Modal's image-build launch protocol (modal_image_build_start.py) runs only when IMAGE_BUILD_MODE=true: after the provider binds the session it reads one 64-hex callback token line on stdin, builds the provider-neutral RepoImageBuildCallback from env, and runs the supervisor with it; a shutdown while waiting cancels cleanly.

Auxiliary services are best-effort and gated by env: code-server starts when CODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is set (port CODE_SERVER_PORT default 8080), the web terminal (ttyd on localhost:7681 + Bun proxy on TTYD_PROXY_PORT default 7680) starts when TERMINAL_ENABLED is set, and the browser desktop (Xvfb + fluxbox + x11vnc localhost:5900 + websockify noVNC default 6080) starts when VNC_PASSWORD is set; the VNC password is stored in /tmp/oi-vnc-password in VNC's fixed-key TripleDES format at mode 0600 with O_NOFOLLOW, and the supervisor turns their start/restart failures into warnings while OpenCode and the bridge are load-bearing.

All sandbox runtime processes emit structured single-line JSON logs to stdout (log_config.py: level/service/component/event/ts plus extra fields, exception type/message/stack truncated to 2000 chars); both the entrypoint and the bridge subprocess call configure_logging().

RuntimeConfig.from_env reads the configuration from process environment only: SESSION_CONFIG (JSON session contract), CONTROL_PLANE_URL (must be HTTPS except loopback dev URLs), SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN, SANDBOX_ID, REPO_OWNER/REPO_NAME, VCS_HOST; the pydantic SessionConfig model round-trips config into SESSION_CONFIG and silently drops unknown keys, so new wire fields must be added to the model or they never reach the sandbox.
